feed.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean

entry.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
entry.summary:
Lean’s capabilities in formalizing and verifying mathematical proofs offer intriguing opportunities for improving cryptographic protocols. Despite the challenges associated with bitcoin, particularly the limitations of fuzzing-based approaches for ensuring security, attempts to innovate in this space are commendable. Batch signature verification emerges as a promising avenue, especially considering its potential impact on computational efficiency within blockchain systems.
While secp256k1 operations, fundamental to many cryptographic applications in blockchains, remain computationally intensive within STARK-based proofs, advancements in hardware acceleration—such as those available through [RiscZero](https://www.risczero.com)—are beginning to alleviate some of these burdens. This opens up the possibility of batch-verifying all Schnorr signatures using a single multi-scalar multiplication, not just at the level of individual blocks but potentially across the entire blockchain. Such an approach could vastly reduce verification overhead, making it feasible even for lightweight clients like mobile devices.
Verification time, which currently exhibits an O(log² n) complexity similar to that seen in communication and proof size, poses a bottleneck. The recorded verification time of 72 seconds highlights the need for further optimization. Techniques akin to Risc Zero's "shrink wrap," where a Groth16 proof is used to verify the output of a STARK verifier, present an innovative solution. This method dramatically reduces verification time by shifting the computational burden to the proof generation phase, making real-time verification almost trivial. While some sectors of the community may prioritize QR-based methods, alternative approaches continue to show significant promise for enhancing scalability and accessibility in blockchain systems.
